assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicted (Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model) and then observed flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity at the magic angle, opening a tunable platform for strongly correlated electrons. Conceptually clear, original and now a field of its own; the interplay of interactions, geometry and disorder is attractive from a many-body perspective.
assessment.attribution: The theory-experiment pairing is natural: MacDonald and Bistritzer for the flat-band prediction, Jarillo-Herrero for the 2018 correlated-insulator and superconducting observations. Other groups contributed to the experimental wave, so a three-person split omits some credit.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduced the phenomenology within a few years; the field is mature enough for recognition, though the microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated.
uncertainties: Breadth of experimental credit beyond one named experimentalist.
I rely on my own recollection of the chronology and have not verified it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, deliver fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and are driving a redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. A clear instrument-level breakthrough with broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Ye led the push in accuracy, stability and many-body clock physics. Two names fit the supplied credit cleanly; other contributors are not in the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Several independent laboratories reach comparable performance, the interpretation is stable and the second redefinition is under discussion; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes (2005, 2012) may be seen as incremental by some members.
Allocation relative to related clock work is partly unclear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 discovery of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS completed the Standard Model and confirmed the mechanism recognised in 2013. The experimental achievement, in detector design, statistics and analysis, is of lasting importance.
assessment.attribution: The three named people are widely identified as founding leaders of ATLAS and CMS. Credit in collaborations of thousands is intrinsically hard to allocate, and a three-person limit is a recognised tension; the supplied names are a plausible, defensible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by two experiments and by later coupling measurements; the interpretation is very stable. Recognition is timely, even somewhat overdue given the 2013 theory prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee is comfortable honouring leadership roles in large collaborations.
Individual scientific contributions are less specific than for a small-team experiment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation defines a universality class for nonequilibrium interface growth, tied to random matrices (Tracy-Widom statistics), integrability and many physical systems. Takeuchi's liquid-crystal experiments gave a striking quantitative confirmation. A clean, originating idea in nonequilibrium statistical physics, a field I know well.
assessment.attribution: Kardar, Parisi and Zhang wrote the 1986 paper; Giorgio Parisi is not among the supplied credited names, so the theory side here is only Kardar and Zhang, an incomplete picture of the original credit. Takeuchi supplies the experimental confirmation of the exact distributions.
assessment.maturity: Exact solutions by several theorists and repeated experiments have confirmed the picture; the interpretation is stable. Timing is good, but the exact-solution contributors are also part of the story.
uncertainties: Credit is incomplete because Parisi is absent from the supplied names.
Physical impact beyond the specific class may be judged narrower than other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the Jaksch-Zoller Hubbard proposal to the Greiner-Bloch Mott-insulator transition and quantum-gas microscopy, created controllable quantum simulators for many-body models. Original and influential across condensed matter and statistical physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller supplied key theoretical proposals; Bloch and Greiner led pivotal experiments. Esslinger is also credited, so choosing three requires a judgment between bosonic and fermionic realisations; I favour the founding proposal and the Mott-insulator demonstration.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and maturing; quantum advantage over classical simulation is still being demonstrated, but the experimental foundations are solid.
uncertainties: Choice among four credited names is difficult.
Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize and with other quantum-simulation candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's observation of a diffuse high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux, of TXS 0506+056 and of the Galactic plane established neutrino astronomy using a gigaton Antarctic ice detector. A major instrumental and discovery milestone.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the IceCube concept and collaboration; Spiering was a leading figure in the Baikal and AMANDA-IceCube lineage. Contributions of the wider collaboration and earlier pioneers complicate a fair two-person recognition.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed by multiple analyses and source associations are building, though the origin of most neutrinos is unknown. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Attribution to two individuals from a large collaboration is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kane-Mele proposal and the HgTe observation of the quantum spin Hall effect established topological insulators, a conceptual advance in classifying matter by topology with large impact on later work.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the original theoretical insight and Molenkamp's group the experimental demonstration; other theorists (e.g. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang; Fu and Kane in three dimensions) are not in the supplied names, so the allocation is partial.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed experimentally; however, the 2016 prize on topological phases already recognised related ideas, which may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize and with other topological candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Event Horizon Telescope delivered the first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A*, directly probing strong-field gravity near black holes. A striking demonstration, although the precision of the physics tests is still modest.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow-imaging concept, Doeleman led the global VLBI effort and Zensus built European VLBI capacity. With a collaboration of hundreds, any triple is inherently selective.
assessment.maturity: Images are consistent across epochs and sources, but reconstruction relies on modelling and priors and independent verification beyond the EHT itself is limited; slightly premature for physics impact.
uncertainties: Fair allocation in a very large collaboration is uncertain.
